name: Fencing

seo.title: Fence Companies in Sioux Falls, SD
seo.description: Building or replacing a fence in Sioux Falls? Local guides on permits, height limits, materials for our winters, property lines and what to ask a fence company.

intro:
Every fence in Sioux Falls needs a permit, and that surprises a lot of homeowners. Height limits depend on where the fence sits, and covenants in many neighborhoods add their own rules.

Get the permit, the property line and the post depth right, and the material choice becomes the fun part.
tips: Ask who pulls the fence permit and schedules the final inspection, since the City requires both.
Confirm where the property line is before anyone digs; the City's fence guide says a licensed surveyor should locate it.
Ask how deep posts are set and how they handle frost heave in our clay soil.
Check your neighborhood covenants for height, style and material rules before you choose.
Call 811 before digging, and ask the contractor to confirm utilities are marked.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit to build a fence in Sioux Falls?
faqs.a: Yes. According to the City of Sioux Falls, you need a permit to build, move, replace or repair a fence. The City's fence pamphlet lists the permit fee as $20, and a final inspection is required after the fence is finished.

faqs.q: How tall can my fence be?
faqs.a: It depends on which yard it is in. The City's residential fence guide allows fences up to four feet in front yards, with taller limits in side and rear yards. Check the current rules with the Zoning Office before you buy materials.

faqs.q: How do I know where my property line is?
faqs.a: Do not guess from the old fence. The City's fence guide says property lines should be located by a licensed surveyor. Pins or a survey save expensive mistakes.

faqs.q: Which fence material lasts best here?
faqs.a: Wood, vinyl, aluminum, steel and chain link each handle cold, wind and sun differently. Ask each contractor how their product handles frost heave, wind load and upkeep.

faqs.q: How long is a fence permit good for?
faqs.a: The City's fence pamphlet says permits expire six months after they are issued, and extensions are available from the Zoning Office.

faqs.q: Can I build a fence in winter?
faqs.a: Sometimes, if the ground can be dug and set. Ask how they handle frozen soil and whether posts will be set properly before snow.
